question: Can linear temporal logic be evaluated by one algebra-generic differentiable engine while making the semantic laws, computational cost, and backward credit behavior of each candidate algebra explicit?

key_findings.claim: A small algebra interface is sufficient to interpret the same temporal-logic syntax over Boolean, fuzzy, robustness, parametric, and lifted semantics.
key_findings.evidence: The evaluator defines logical connectives through four primitive algebra operations and derives temporal operators from scans, folds, and interval spans. Boolean evaluation is recovered as one exact instance, while Product, Goedel, Lukasiewicz, Robustness, LSE, and parametric t-norm families reuse the same structural recursion.

key_findings.claim: Common differentiable fuzzy semantics make unavoidable tradeoffs among logical laws and gradient usefulness; the paper classifies the main failures as selection, saturation, or decay.
key_findings.evidence: Extremum-based Goedel and robustness semantics send credit to one selected input; Lukasiewicz-style clamping saturates; Product-style multiplication decays through long formulas and traces. The paper ties this trichotomy to the ordinal-sum classification of continuous t-norms and mechanically audits idempotence, absorption, distributivity, complementation, associativity, unitality, and monotonicity.

key_findings.claim: Algebraic structure converts serial temporal reductions into parallel kernels without hard-coding one semantic choice.
key_findings.evidence: Associativity permits parallel prefix scans; idempotent extrema map to cumulative min/max; Product maps to cumulative products; LSE maps to log-cumulative-exp; and Archimedean t-norms factor through a generator so running meets become cumulative sums in generator coordinates. The general until operator still uses a triangular T-by-T window construction, but each row can be swept in parallel.

key_findings.claim: LSE preserves dense, normalized gradients but produces duration-dependent and potentially unsound temporal verdicts.
key_findings.evidence: Its backward shares are softmax weights that sum to one; for a length-T constant trace, individual credit decays harmonically as 1/T rather than exponentially. However, repeated evidence shifts globally and finally verdicts with trace duration, eventually allowing safety or liveness signs to flip even when every tick's semantic status is unchanged.

key_findings.claim: A lifted monoidal state makes irreducibly variadic means compatible with parallel temporal evaluation, and mellowmax is the only audited candidate in the paper that combines duration-invariant verdicts with dense, smooth, normalized, non-negative credit.
key_findings.evidence: The State abstraction stores interval summaries with associative combine and a neutral element, enabling logarithmic-depth prefix sweeps. Boltzmann averaging initially supplies dense credit but fails monotonicity because values also choose their own weights. Replacing it with mellowmax preserves LSE's softmax gradient, makes a constant trace evaluate to the same value at any duration, and passes monotonicity, involution, De Morgan duality, and the embed-readout section law; associativity and lattice laws still fail in carrier space.

method.core_idea: Separate temporal-logic syntax from quantitative semantics, encode the latter as interchangeable PyTorch algebras, and use executable property tests to audit both forward laws and backward credit.
method.mechanism: A structural-recursive LTL evaluator delegates propositional operations to an Algebra and temporal reductions to generic scans and interval spans. Folded algebras can override reductions with law-licensed vectorized kernels. For non-associative variadic means, a Lifted algebra embeds each tensor into an associative monoidal State, performs parallel prefix or window combination there, and reads a verdict back. Property-based tests search for counterexamples to algebraic laws, while automatic differentiation reveals gradient sparsity, saturation, decay, sign, and normalization.
assumptions: Finite traces are sufficient for the intended differentiable-control and sequence-model use cases.
An involutive negation is acceptable for deriving lifted joins from lifted meets.
The embed-readout section law preserves individual truth values even when readout forgets state needed for associative recombination.
Randomized property-based audits are useful executable specifications but do not substitute for formal proofs of every law.
Gradient density and normalization are useful proxies for trainability; the paper does not run an end-to-end policy-learning benchmark to establish downstream optimization gains.

techniques.role: Keeps formula traversal independent of truth-value carrier and connective implementation.
Searches automatically for counterexamples to idempotence, absorption, distributivity, complementation, monotonicity, unitality, and related contracts.
Factors Archimedean t-norms through additive generators so serial folds become vectorized cumulative sums.
Combines interval summaries at power-of-two offsets, reducing temporal dependency depth while retaining a generic associative state interface.
Moves a non-associative verdict operator into an associative summary space with sufficient statistics and a neutral element.
Carries a running maximum and rescaled weights so Boltzmann or mellowmax summaries combine without numerical overflow.
Classifies backward behavior as selection, saturation, decay, or dense normalized credit rather than judging semantics only by forward values.

evaluations.setting: Mechanically audited catalogue of 16 Boolean, fuzzy, robustness, LSE, Boltzmann, and mellowmax semantics
evaluations.metric: Logical laws, differentiability, trainable parameters, unitality, monotonicity, and gradient-credit class
evaluations.result: Only Boolean is a full lattice; standard differentiable t-norms exhibit selection, saturation, or decay; LSE and mellowmax have dense credit, but only mellowmax is monotone and idempotent in the reported audit
evaluations.baseline: Boolean semantics and standard fuzzy/robustness algebras

evaluations.setting: Length-T constant traces under LSE and mellowmax
evaluations.metric: Duration dependence and per-tick gradient share
evaluations.result: LSE credit remains dense with approximately 1/T shares but its verdict changes with T; mellowmax retains the same softmax gradient profile and returns the constant value independently of T
evaluations.baseline: Extremum semantics select one tick; Product gradients decay exponentially; Lukasiewicz saturates

evaluations.result: Associative State sweeps use power-of-two prefix combination; the general until window representation remains quadratic in T
evaluations.baseline: Fallback Python folds and scans have linear serial depth; naive independent window reduction can be cubic

evaluations.result: Boltzmann fails because raising a low value can increase its weight and lower the weighted average; mellowmax has non-negative softmax partial derivatives and passes monotonicity

limitations: Reviewer-identified: evaluation is an algebraic and implementation audit, not an end-to-end experiment showing improved policy learning, control synthesis, or neural sequence training.

Reviewer-identified: property-based testing can find counterexamples but cannot prove universal equalities over real-valued tensor domains; several claims rely on established theory or informal derivation rather than machine proofs.
Reviewer-identified: the general until implementation retains O(T^2) window storage, which can dominate long-trace workloads despite parallel scans.

Reviewer-identified: mellowmax sacrifices associativity in carrier space, the residuum, absorption, distributivity, and complementation; emulating top as an abstaining State member is not the same as possessing a true carrier-level unit.
Reviewer-identified: behavior at finite precision, extreme trainable temperature, empty windows, and mixed dtypes/devices may diverge from the ideal algebraic audit.
Reviewer-identified: finite-trace end semantics pad next with bottom, an explicit pessimistic convention that may not fit every monitoring application.
failure_modes: Extremum semantics backpropagate through only one atom-time cell, starving all other candidate repairs.
Nilpotent t-norms clamp long conjunctions to a plateau and erase gradients.
Strict unit-interval t-norms multiply many subunit values, causing both verdicts and gradients to vanish with trace or syntax depth.
LSE can declare a long uniformly unsafe trace safe, or liveness satisfied without a true witness, because its unnormalized log-sum-exp depends on duration.
Boltzmann aggregation can be non-monotone because increasing a weak witness changes both its vote and its voting weight.
As mellowmax temperature hardens toward infinity, its dense gradient collapses toward one-hot selection.
A lifted mean mishandles padding unless distinguished truth values are explicitly mapped to abstaining monoidal states.
reusable_insights: Audit differentiable symbolic operators twice: forward logical behavior and backward credit assignment can favor opposite designs.
Treat executable fallback implementations as semantic specifications; optimized overrides can be checked against them automatically.
Non-associative outputs may still admit associative parallel computation when embedded into a richer sufficient-statistic state.
Coordinate changes can preserve forward algebra while radically changing gradients, so isomorphic semantics need not be optimization-equivalent.
Normalize repeated soft aggregation as a mean when repeated identical evidence should not change the verdict.
A neutral element can be represented as abstention in state space even when no finite carrier value acts as a true unit.
open_questions: Does mellowmax temporal supervision improve sample efficiency or constraint satisfaction in real neural-policy training compared with robustness, LSE, and smooth STL baselines?
Can general until be evaluated with subquadratic memory while preserving algebra genericity and differentiability?
What temperature schedules preserve dense credit early and sound, sharp verdicts late without causing selection collapse?
Can formal proof assistants replace randomized law audits while retaining executable PyTorch implementations?
How should infinite-trace, streaming, or uncertain-horizon semantics be lifted into associative monitor states?
Is there a semantics with carrier-level unitality, monotonicity, duration invariance, and dense normalized credit, or is a stronger impossibility result available?

competitive_landscape.title: Backpropagation through Signal Temporal Logic Specifications: Infusing Logical Structure into Gradient-Based Methods
competitive_landscape.difference: STLCG compiles standard quantitative STL robustness into computation graphs for robotics and backpropagation. This paper instead makes the temporal evaluator algebra-generic, audits many semantics and their gradients, and introduces lifted monoidal reductions rather than committing to one robustness algebra.

competitive_landscape.title: A Smooth Robustness Measure of Signal Temporal Logic for Symbolic Control
competitive_landscape.difference: Gilpin et al. design one smooth, sound, asymptotically complete approximation for symbolic control. This paper emphasizes a reusable semantic interface and the tradeoff between logical soundness, duration invariance, computational laws, and gradient density across an entire catalogue.

competitive_landscape.title: On Robustness Metrics for Learning STL Tasks
competitive_landscape.difference: Varnai and Dimarogonas derive desirable robustness properties and introduce a learning-oriented metric with a control case study. This work gives an executable cross-algebra audit and derives mellowmax through backward-credit requirements and monoidal lifting, but does not supply an equivalent downstream learning study.

competitive_landscape.title: Analyzing Differentiable Fuzzy Logic Operators
competitive_landscape.difference: van Krieken et al. formally and empirically analyze differentiable fuzzy operators in semi-supervised learning and introduce sigmoidal implications. This paper extends the audit to temporal folds, parallel execution, lifted variadic states, and duration-sensitive gradient behavior.

novelty_assessment: Author claim: telos provides an algebra-generic differentiable LTL engine, an executable contract for its admissible semantics, and a lifted mellowmax algebra that unifies duration-invariant verdicts with live credit. Primary prior work already supplies differentiable STL graphs, smooth robustness functions, learning-oriented robustness axioms, and broad fuzzy-operator audits. Reviewer inference: the novel contribution is the software-abstraction and functional-programming synthesis—especially monoidal lifting of variadic temporal aggregation and the joint forward/backward audit—not the individual ingredients of fuzzy semantics, scan algorithms, mellowmax, or property testing. The absence of downstream learning experiments limits evidence that the proposed balance is practically superior.
reviewer_notes: The full paper is a constructive technical essay rather than a conventional benchmark paper. Quantitative statements are limited to analytical scaling and gradient profiles and were checked against pages 5-13. Competitive mechanisms and identifiers were verified on primary arXiv records. Claims that mellowmax 'works' mean it passes the paper's audited forward/backward criteria, not that it has yet won an end-to-end learning benchmark.
